body:
OBSERVED AT RUNTIME 2026-08-23 on a container running the published `:dev` image, with three
probe users and both directions controlled.

Classic gates browser reading on `role_viewer()`: the "Read now" CTA renders only under
`{% if entry.reader_list and current_user.role_viewer() %}` (`cps/templates/detail.html:630`),
and both server read routes are `@viewer_required` — `/show/<id>/<fmt>` (`cps/web.py:2344`) and
`/read/<id>/<fmt>` (`cps/web.py:3377`), where `viewer_required` aborts 403
(`cps/web.py:253-260`).

The SPA does neither. Its read CTA is computed from formats alone with no role check
(`frontend/src/pages/BookDetail.tsx:412`, via `getPrimaryReadTarget`), and its EPUB reader fetches
`format.download_url` (`frontend/src/pages/Reader.tsx:1002`), which the serializer builds as
`/download/{id}/{fmt}/{name}` (`cps/api/serializers.py:309`) — a route gated by
`download_required`, i.e. `role_download()` ONLY (`cps/web.py:243-250`, `:2409-2413`).
`viewer` is serialized to the client (`cps/api/serializers.py:92`) and is not read anywhere under
`frontend/src`.

Measured, book 197, same instance, same moment:

    user roles              /read/<id>/epub   /show/<id>/epub   /download/<id>/epub/...
    download, NO viewer          403               403                200  (271,673 bytes)
    viewer, NO download          200               200                403
    download + viewer            200               200                200

So the two UIs disagree in BOTH directions, and the second one is the sharp end:

1. download-without-viewer — classic refuses to let them read in the browser. The new UI shows
   "Read now" (confirmed in the rendered a11y tree) and `/app/read/197` fetched the EPUB with
   HTTP 200. The `viewer` bit has no effect on EPUB reading in the new UI.

2. viewer-without-download — the exact user the role exists for. Classic serves them the book.
   The new UI renders **"Could not load the book file (403)"**. Its reader cannot serve the one
   role that means "may read in the browser".

Control that matters: the allowed user (download+viewer) produced the SAME empty epub.js iframe
under `contentDocument.innerText` as the denied one, so that emptiness is my instrument, not the
permission — the 403 error string and the wire statuses are the evidence, not the iframe.

Fix shape: the reader must not read through the download route. Either give the SPA reader a
viewer-gated content endpoint (or route it through `/show`, which already carries the right gate),
and gate the read CTA on `me.role.viewer` so the control matches what the server will do. Deciding
which role should govern in-browser reading is a policy call — classic's answer is `viewer`, and
whatever is chosen, the UI, the reader's fetch and the route guard must agree. Compare F-2f48b9:
same defect class (a control gated on a different bit than its own backend), same both-directions
signature.

--- WIDENED 2026-08-23, same session, same instance ---

It is not only reading. The SPA ignores `download` as well, so the SAME viewer-only user is shown
three download links that all answer 403. Classic gates that list on `role_download()`
(`cps/templates/detail.html:642,919`); the SPA renders it unconditionally
(`frontend/src/pages/BookDetail.tsx:455`).

Rendered, book 197, viewer-only user (no download), both UIs at the same moment:

    Classic /book/197       download links: (none)              read link: /read/197/epub
    New UI  /app/book/197   download links: EPUB, KEPUB, MOBI   "Read now" -> /app/read/197
                            all three 403                       which renders 403

Control: the same Classic page as admin renders three download links plus the read link, so
Classic's omission is the gate working, not a broken page.

And the read affordance is missing its gate on the CARDS too, not just book detail:
`frontend/src/components/BookCard.tsx:57,202` also derives it from `getPrimaryReadTarget` alone, so
every card in the library carries it.

Restated root cause: **the SPA renders book affordances without consulting either of the two roles
that govern them.** One fix, one place to get right — the affordance set has to be derived from
`me.role`, and the reader needs a content path gated on `viewer` rather than borrowing the
download-gated route.

Policy resolved: the project goal is to replace the classic UI entirely, so Classic's rules are the
reference — `viewer` governs reading, `download` governs downloading. Not an intentional
simplification.


--- SHARPEST INSTANCE, OBSERVED AT RUNTIME 2026-08-23: the SPA's OWN api serves comic pages with no
viewer gate at all ---

The earlier halves are the SPA borrowing a wrongly-gated classic route. This one is different and
worse: a first-party `/api/v1` endpoint serves book content and never checks `viewer`.

`cps/api/comic.py:68-70` and `:83-85` — both `/books/<id>/comic` and `/books/<id>/comic/<page>`
carry only `@login_required_if_no_ano`. Classic's comic reader is `/read/<id>/<comic format>`,
which is `@viewer_required` (`cps/web.py:3377`).

Measured, book 19 (the seed's only CBZ):

    user roles            classic /read/19/cbz   /api/v1/books/19/comic   /api/v1/books/19/comic/0
    download, NO viewer          403                     200                200  (4,951 bytes)
    viewer, NO download          200                     200                200  (4,951 bytes)

The viewer-only row is the control and it is correct — the endpoint should serve that user, and it
does. The defect is the first row: a user classic refuses is served the actual page image bytes.
So this is a one-directional over-permission, not an inversion, and unlike the download-route half
it cannot be explained away as "they could have downloaded it anyway" — this account has download,
but the point is that `viewer` is the bit classic uses to decide in-browser reading and this
endpoint does not consult it.

I enumerated every content-serving endpoint under `cps/api/` independently (`send_file` /
`send_from_directory` / `make_response` across `cps/api/*.py`) and `comic.py` is the ONLY one; every
other format is served by the classic `/download`, `/show` and `/read` routes. So the fix surface is
bounded: one API module plus the reader's content path.
title: The viewer role is inverted in the New UI reader: it blocks the users it exists for and admits the ones classic refuses
